qualification: Native ARM build, nonroot read-only import/artifact execution, and exact installed-image scans are required; base/image metadata alone does not qualify a release.

bundledUndici.qualification: Complete official package replacement only; npm 12.2.1 upstream is unchanged otherwise and has not released this fix. Build compares every other npm file against its original tarball and verifies the replacement bytes, node-gyp resolution and declared semver range.

rendererProvenance.qualification: Unqualified source installation pins. Exact ARM image must pass observed no-network/non-root/read-only/no-credentials/limited child sandbox and Office/PDF corpus acceptance before renderer availability.

clamavSourcePreparation.scope: Authenticate the official ClamAV 1.5.4 release asset, prepare a pinned aarch64 build/development closure and a build-only compiler stage, replace the vulnerable Wolfi clamav-1.5 payload coherently, and record a truthful source-built inventory and coverage path. No build, no probe, no scan, no publication.

authentication.signatureFormat: OpenPGP detached signature, v4, RSA, digest SHA1, signature class 0x00 (binary document)
authentication.keyPath: src/manual/cisco-talos.gpg in Cisco-Talos/clamav-documentation, linked from docs.clamav.net/manual/Installing.html
authentication.issuerMatchesKey: the signing key id embedded in the detached signature (707F0DB480836771) is the key id of the vendor-published key
authentication.metadataVersusActual: the release metadata digest and the sha256 computed from the downloaded bytes are equal; the metadata digest is not treated as the verification, the computed sha256 over the received bytes is
authentication.vendoredRustDependencies: .cargo/vendor with 290 vendored crate directories plus .cargo/config.toml mapping crates-io and the two Cisco git sources to the vendored tree, so cargo builds offline

imageProvenance.builtFrom: the authenticated upstream release asset, not a distribution package
imageProvenance.installedBy: apps/runtime/Dockerfile, stage clamav-source-build, copied into the runtime stage from /tmp/meri-clamav-out
imageProvenance.installedInventory: /usr/share/meri/clamav-component-inventory.txt (sha256 of the installed executables in usr/bin and of the ClamAV and freshclam shared libraries in usr/lib: the payload's executable and shared-library surface, not every file the image carries; re-checked against the installed bytes in the runtime stage and verified again by the image build probe)
imageProvenance.installedInventorySha256: written into the image's provenance at build time from the inventory file itself and checked by the image build probe, so the provenance cannot cover a different inventory
imageProvenance.libraryRelationships: built with ENABLE_SHARED_LIB=ON and ENABLE_STATIC_LIB=OFF, so the payload ships shared libraries only: the installed tools load libclamav and libfreshclam from /usr/lib at runtime, and libclamav links the pinned closure's zlib, openssl, libxml2, pcre2, bzip2 and json-c as the image provides them. Presence and version are asserted in the runtime stage; linkage and ABI remain unverified until a real ARM build.
imageProvenance.coverageBinding: the image build probe in infra/product-preview/image-build.sh executes python3.13 /usr/share/meri/clamav_component_coverage.py --bind against this image's own clamscan, this inventory and this provenance, and fails the build when any of them disagree
imageProvenance.qualification: built, installed, probed and scanned image state is unproven until a separately allocated ARM build, probe and scan

This is an unresolved distribution-input gap, recorded rather than papered over.
rustToolchain.verification: detached signature over the toolchain archive verified with the release key: exit 0; the published .sha256 and the signed stable channel manifest name the same sha256 the downloaded bytes hash to

buildClosure.source: resolved from the retained vendor-signed index 5c84e4b835a811c1624d9692f011df3de446c8011be4dedaabf6f3dbf41ec536 and pinned by the sha256 of each downloaded official archive; includes the 35 transitive packages selected by apk in the compiler-stage installation
buildClosure.sizeChecks: every downloaded archive length equals the index S: field exactly (0 mismatches)
buildClosure.unresolvedNote: the unresolved tokens are virtual provides (merged-lib/-sbin/-usrsbin) of packages the pinned base already installs (wolfi-baselayout), so no archive is required for them

opensslProviderReconciliation.reason: The development closure staged three mutually exclusive OpenSSL development providers (openssl-dev 3.6.5-r6, openssl-4.0-dev 4.0.3-r0 and openssl-4.0-dev 4.0.3-r8), so the offline install aborted with 151 file-ownership collisions against the base-owned openssl-4.0-dev-4.0.3-r0. The staged set now carries exactly one OpenSSL development provider.
opensslProviderReconciliation.removed: openssl-dev-3.6.5-r6 (16355385 B): it duplicates the usr/include/openssl, usr/lib/libcrypto.*, usr/lib/libssl.*, pkgconfig and cmake paths the pinned base already owns, which is the collision the build hit. openssl-4.0-dev-4.0.3-r0 (16510022 B): base-installed already, provides none of the development capabilities, and is superseded by the selected 4.0.3-r8 of the same package name.
opensslProviderReconciliation.selectionBasis: curl-dev and ngtcp2-dev depend on openssl-4.0-dev by name and on pc:openssl. In the retained signed index only the 4.0 development records from 4.0.3-r1 onward provide openssl-dev/pc:openssl/pc:libssl/pc:libcrypto, and the base-installed 4.0.3-r0 provides none of them, so 4.0.3-r8 is the only provider of those capabilities in the series the staged libs (openssl-4.0-libssl/-libcrypto 4.0.3-r8) and the pinned base belong to. It has the same package name as the base-owned 4.0.3-r0, so apk applies a version upgrade instead of a path-ownership takeover.
opensslProviderReconciliation.retained: openssl-3.6-libcrypto/-libssl 3.6.5-r6 stay staged because libldap-2.6 requires so:libcrypto.so.3 and so:libssl.so.3. The base-owned openssl-4.0-dev-4.0.3-r0 pin was removed too: the pinned base already installs that revision, the requested 4.0.3-r8 upgrades the same package name, and keeping both revisions in the declared closure would declare a set apk cannot install.
opensslProviderReconciliation.buildValidation: Source checks only; a rebuilt image is not claimed.

ctestGateCorrection.observed: AWS build 75b91bdb (b3fb9ca7): ClamAV ctest reported 67 percent passed, 2 of 6 tests failed after the patch applied and the whole tree compiled - libclamav ran 1239 checks with 4 failures (check_clamav.c 1963/1981/1999/2017, SHIFT_JIS and UTF-16BE/LE to UTF8) and clamscan reported Ran 0 tests / NO TESTS RAN
ctestGateCorrection.cause: Two pinned-environment gaps, not ClamAV defects. cli_codepage_to_utf8 (libclamav/entconv.c 817-1058) converts through the system iconv when HAVE_ICONV is set, and the pinned glibc-2.44 archive carries 22 payload files and no /usr/lib/gconv at all, so iconv_open for SHIFT_JIS and UTF-16 fails. Separately, unit_tests/CMakeLists.txt 355-405 registers the clamscan test as the directory clamscan (21 modules in 1.5.4), and with pytest absent CMake falls back to PythonTest_COMMAND = python -m unittest, which imports that directory as an empty namespace package and collects nothing; the single-file clamd, freshclam, libclamav_rust and sigtool suites passed, which is why only the directory-shaped suite reported zero tests
ctestGateCorrection.correction: Stage and install the retained index's glibc-2.44-iconv (usr/lib/gconv with SJIS, libJIS, libJISX0213, UTF-16, UTF-32 and gconv-modules) in the existing development install, and install pytest with its 11 pinned dependencies after the pinned interpreter so CMake selects -m pytest -v. No test is skipped, filtered, excluded or disabled: ENABLE_TESTS=ON and ctest --output-on-failure are unchanged
ctestGateCorrection.provenance: each archive fetched from its pinned packages.wolfi.dev/os/aarch64 URL, sha256 computed from the fetched bytes, and its length, package name and version verified against the retained vendor-signed index and against the archive's own .PKGINFO; the retained index is an apk v2 index whose C: field is not an sha256, so the pin is the downloaded digest rather than an index-transcribed one
ctestGateCorrection.buildValidation: Source checks only: staging lines, install requests, assertion loop, lock members and closure totals are verified textually and against the index. apk installation, iconv conversion, pytest collection and the 1239-case run remain the next ARM build's obligation.

compilerClosureCorrection.reason: The original development repository omitted packages selected by the signed index during offline installation, including dependencies already staged only for the runtime. Stage those exact selected versions in the development repository as well.
compilerClosureCorrection.buildValidation: Source checks only; a rebuilt image is not claimed.

install.offlineEnforced: the whole compiler stage runs under RUN --network=none, with the development closure mounted read-only from the build-only staging repository and apk --no-network: the vendored crate tree inside the release asset and FindRust's offline mode are the mechanism, and the network-none guard is what enforces it for configure, cargo, the build and ctest
install.whyThisPrefix: apps/runtime/uploads/native-sandbox.mjs pins the child sandbox's absolute tool paths (/usr/bin/clamscan, /usr/bin/tesseract, /usr/bin/pdftoppm, /usr/bin/python3.13), so the payload is installed where that contract already points and no PATH ordering decides which ClamAV runs
install.buildOnlyEvidence: the compiler, the Rust toolchain, the development headers and the build tree exist only in stages that are not the exported stage; no runtime instruction carries them
install.unitTests: the project's own unit-test target is built (ENABLE_TESTS=ON) and run with ctest in the build stage, so a future build executes real ClamAV unit tests before the payload is installed
install.componentInventory: /usr/share/meri/clamav-component-inventory.txt, written in the build stage from the payload's installed executables (usr/bin, usr/sbin) and its shared libraries (usr/lib/libclam*.so*, usr/lib/libfreshclam*.so*) and re-checked with sha256sum -c against the installed bytes in the runtime stage, so the record is bound to what the image carries. It is the component's executable and library surface, not every file the image carries: the shipped configuration files and the runtime database directories are not hashed.

replacedPayload.method: removed, not shadowed: no Wolfi clamav-1.5 package is installed, so no distribution package record and no 1.5.2 payload remains, and the runtime asserts that no clamav-1.5 package is installed
replacedPayload.whyStillStaged: the 190-archive pinned staging closure, its order, its URLs and its checksums are preserved unchanged; these eight archives are simply no longer requested by any install, so their bytes are neither installed nor present as a payload

coverage.method: documented source-range recognition bound to the actual built-image component version, with bounded known-vulnerable, known-fixed and binding controls; it is evidence for the advisory-feed gap, not scanner detection, and it does not weaken the retained HIGH==0 CRITICAL==0 gate
coverage.outcomes: each advisory and release yields one of fixed, affected, not-affected or unknown; only fixed and not-affected pass, so an affected or otherwise undescribed release always fails closed, and every advisory's documented affected range is retained in the table rather than inferred from an absent release note
coverage.binding: the coverage result is bound to the built image by the retained image build probe (infra/product-preview/image-build.sh, the network-isolated common docker probe array): python3.13 -I -B /usr/share/meri/clamav_component_coverage.py --bind reads the version from the image's own clamscan, verifies every file the recorded inventory lists against the installed bytes, requires the provenance to declare that same version and to carry the inventory's own sha256, and fails the build (non-zero exit, as every other probe does) when any of them disagrees. The checker and the advisory table are copied into the image from the verified source tree, so the probe measures the image's own bytes rather than a host-side fixture.
coverage.scannerFeedGap: the retained scan records only CVSS score/vector/package name/version and no fixed-version metadata, and the vendor feed's declared fixed revision (clamav-1.5 1.5.4-r2) is not published in any Wolfi or Chainguard apk repository for aarch64 or x86_64

uploadNativeProvenance.note: The Wolfi APKINDEX is a rolling live file, so the frozen index hash above is only a per-retrieval audit record; the pinned .apk archives are the authoritative immutable artifacts. Every recorded .apk sha256 was computed from the downloaded official archive, and every download length matched the index S: field exactly.
uploadNativeProvenance.closure: The whole transitive native closure of the seven upload archives (and of the python and renderer layers) is staged inside one local apk repository: 190 official aarch64 archives pinned by exact URL and sha256 in the Dockerfile ADD --checksum list and in systemPackages, beside the retained vendor-signed index recorded above. The three native layers install with `apk add --no-cache --no-network --repository /tmp/meri-native-repo --update-cache <name>=<version>`, so apk admits every archive through that index signature and its recorded package identity and never through a local file path or --allow-untrusted. This corrects the earlier claim that the previous 88-archive closure installed from local paths: the exact locked command `apk add --no-cache --no-network <pinned archives>` fails with UNTRUSTED signature exit 99, and the previous closure was also incomplete (apk resolves 175 members for these layers; 91 further official archives were added here). The engine library itself moves with the release: so:libclamav.so.12 is provided by clamav-1.5 1.5.2-r7 (the approved scanner binaries stay at the pinned 1.5.2-r0), and the Wolfi clamav-1.5 package hard-depends on clamav-1.5-daemon/-milter/-clamdscan/-db/-libunrar, so those binaries are installed but nothing configures or starts a daemon and no clamd.conf exists. SCRUM-197 update: the three Wolfi clamav-1.5 install requests are removed from the upload layer and the ClamAV payload is now source-built from the authenticated upstream 1.5.4 release asset in the build-only clamav-source-build stage (see clamavSourcePreparation). The eight clamav-1.5 family archives stay in this pinned staging closure byte for byte, with their URLs, checksums and order unchanged, but no install requests them any more: the vulnerable payload is removed rather than shadowed through PATH precedence, and the image asserts that no clamav-1.5 distribution package is installed.

baseInstalledSet.statement: The base image's own installed package set is UNOBSERVED: no pull, manifest inspection or in-image apk info was performed, and no base-installed version is claimed here. The intended effect of this delta is an UPGRADE of the shared C++ runtime to the index-newest revisions the closure pins (libstdc++ 16.2.0-r2, libgcc 16.2.0-r2) while libatomic stays at its approved 16.2.0-r1 pin.
baseInstalledSet.failClosed: Because every upload-layer install names exact archive files, a base digest that already carried a newer revision of any named package makes apk add refuse the older explicit file: the build fails closed instead of silently drifting to a different version.
